rules.title: Good-cause requirement for nonrenewal of residential leases
rules.requirement: A landlord generally may not refuse to renew a residential tenant’s lease, whether written or oral, unless the landlord has good cause. This protection does not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, or transient or seasonal units.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Motels or hotels, transient units, and seasonal units are excluded.
coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental properties except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient units, and seasonal units.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three 
family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, 
regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

rules.title: Security deposit cap and handling requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord who collects a security deposit generally may not collect more than one and one-half months’ rent, and any later annual increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Security deposit money remains the tenant’s property and must be held in trust in a qualifying New Jersey account or investment, depending on the number of units.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; annual increase max 10% of current deposit

coverage.other_unresolvable: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, but generally excludes owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant invokes the law by written request.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted unless the tenant makes the law applicable by written request; the stated deposit-account requirements do not apply to security deposits for seasonal use or rental.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
